criteria.question: on the male CNS: does the reset rule, or completing MN9_R's input, give a synaptic scale that is both functional and stable; is M1's MN9 response specific to the real wiring at 100 draws; and where does the blind-drive reverberation sustain itself?
criteria.plan: docs/gen6_phaseA_DRAFT.md (every definition there, section 'Definitions fixed before registering' wins)

celltypes.built_by: scripts/make_gen6_celltypes.py from the MaleCNS Cell Type Explorer repository

protocol.sweep: per trial: restore, 200 ms silence, 1000 ms drive, 500 ms with every stimulus rate at 0; 10 trials; one network per arm; readouts as Phase 1b's run_sweep_trial

drives.sugar: every LB3b and LB3c cell at 100 Hz
drives.blind: fit/select_wscale.py's drive, as Phase 1b: a fixed 10% (numpy default_rng(0)) of the eligible sensory cells, at 20 Hz
drives.composition: A4 (M3): the stimulated types and the driven set of the blind drive kept, so the network is the same; rate set to 0 for (b) driven cells with superclass ol_sensory or a transmitter (consensusNt, else predictedNt) other than acetylcholine; (c) those, plus types starting ORN_ or HRN_

protocol.ladder: A3 real arm: as M1, 30 trials of 1000 ms at sugar 100 Hz, seed 6100
protocol.null: A3: 100 degree-corrected rewirings (flycns.graph.rewire_null, mode degree_corrected), one 1000 ms trial each under M1; alive iff the null median whole-CNS rate >= 0.1 x the real arm's median (Phase 1b's rule)
protocol.seeds: sweep, drive and cut arms: 6000 + index of (drive, w), shared by every arm at the same (drive, w) (paired, M5); top-ups 7000 + the same index; A3 real 6100; A3 null model 6101 with rewiring seeds 30000 + k, k = 0..99

cells.check: asserted against type == 'MN9' and soma side on the pinned data

mn9.mirror: cells c2 and c4 (B3): applied to load_graph's signed edges (at or above the floor), before the model is built. MN9_R's input is REPLACED by the mirror of MN9_L's: each partner P -> MN9_L (weight w) becomes P' -> MN9_R for every SIMULATED cell P' of P's type on the opposite side (one with at least one edge at or above the floor; adding an edgeless cell would change the simulated cell set), weight w / (number of such cells), kept as a float even below the floor. Side = flycns.graph.infer_side without the soma-x fallback (somaSide, then instance _L/_R); anything else is midline. Untyped, midline and no-match partners stay on P (P -> MN9_R, w). A mirrored edge takes P''s own model sign (the model signs every edge by its sender); if P' has no signed output, P's sign. MN9_R -> MN9_L becomes MN9_L -> MN9_R, with MN9_L's own sign. MN9_R's outputs are unchanged. Repeated (pre, post) pairs are summed. A cell whose only edge went into MN9_R keeps a zero-weight self-edge, so the simulated cell set is unchanged (m5)
mn9.normalise: cells c2b and c4b: MN9_R's existing input weights multiplied by (MN9_L's signed input total / MN9_R's), both from load_graph's edges (M8); partners unchanged

cuts.rule: A4 (B2): applied to load_graph's signed edges; defined by cell type (the committed lists) and the post cell's dominant_roi (data/roi_membership.parquet). A cell whose every edge is cut keeps a zero-weight self-edge, so the simulated cell set equals the uncut one (m5); such a cell has no input at or above the floor and never fires either way. On the pinned data a cut that removes no edge refuses to run
cuts.lh: remove edges with pre an AL PN (type in ALPN) and post dominant_roi in LH(L), LH(R)
cuts.lhmb: as lh, and also edges with pre an AL PN and post type in Kenyon_Cell or post dominant_roi in CA(L), CA(R)
cuts.i: remove every out-edge of cells with type in ALLN whose transmitter (the edge's nt) is acetylcholine
cuts.ii: remove edges with pre of an ALPN type and nt acetylcholine (all cholinergic ALPN types: uniglomerular, the two-glomerulus '+' types and the multiglomerular M_/MZ_/CB types; Jayson's decisions of 18 October), and post type in ALPN or ALLN. GABAergic and glutamatergic PNs are not cut. The synapses removed from the '+' types and from the M_/MZ_/CB types are reported (descriptions, not arms)

thresholds.meaning: FUNCTION (screen): sugar MN9 two-cell-mean interval wholly above responds_hz (lower edge exclusive). FUNCTION-q: of the non-self-sustained sugar trials, the fraction with MN9 > responds_hz is at least function_q_need, with at least function_q_min_trials such trials, else UNRESOLVED. STABILITY (a)/(b): 0 self-sustained trials; (c): blind intervals of whole-CNS rate and fraction active wholly below rate_bar_hz and fraction_bar (PASS iff upper edge < bar; FAIL iff lower edge >= bar). LATERALITY: median sugar LI < li_bar. W*: grid w with at least wstar_min_self_sustained of 10 baseline blind trials self-sustained. A3: PASS iff real > draw (strict) for at least null_pass_draws valid draws (absolute; with fewer valid draws it cannot pass). M9: tail share >= tail_share_factor x drive share. m3: bimodal iff max n_active > bimodal_factor x max(1, min n_active) (the max(1, .) keeps a zero minimum from making every arm with one active trial bimodal), split at the largest gap

decision.viable: a grid w at which FUNCTION (screen), FUNCTION-q and STABILITY (a), (b), (c) all PASS; the decision w is the smallest such w
decision.table: c1 viable: stop for review (Phase 1b's C not replicated). Else c2 viable: mirror at c2's w (c3 reported if also viable). c3 only: v-and-g reset at c3's w. c4 only: both at c4's w. None: C
decision.laterality: M7: an outcome that adopts the mirror (mirror, both) also needs LATERALITY PASS in its cell (c2, c4) at its decision w; otherwise the outcome is H (rule v2 section 2): no default changes; v-and-g, if viable, is reported
decision.top_up: a candidate w (no component FAILs, at least one UNRESOLVED) in a deciding cell names its arm(s) for ONE top-up (seed 7000 + the pair index, 10 trials); the scorer pools the 10 + 10 trials for every component of that arm (STABILITY (a)/(b) then need 0 of 20; FUNCTION-q counts over the 20); after it, UNRESOLVED counts as not passing
decision.provisional: an adopted w is provisional until gen6_rule.md's refine and confirm steps (both nulls) pass

criteria.scoring: fit/gen6_phaseA_score.py, hashed into this registration: B1 decision table over cells 1-4; FUNCTION (screen), FUNCTION-q, STABILITY (a), (b), (c), LATERALITY for c2/c4 (M7); A3 null at 95 of 100 (M4); A4 readings against W* (M1, M2, M9); the top-up rule; every verdict as the draft defines it

Q1: The v-and-g reset makes the male blind drive stable at some w, by itself
Q2: The MN9_R correction brings male laterality below 0.8
Q4: the antennal-lobe tail persists after both projection cuts (they do not stop it by the M1 rule)
Q5: No cell is viable, so the outcome stays C
Q6: At least one in-AL cut stops it by the M1 rule

definitions.self_sustained: per trial: whole-CNS rate in the last half of the tail >= 0.1 x the rate during the drive, and >= 0.01 Hz (Phase 1b, fit/shiu2024_phase1b.py:474)
definitions.a3_statistic: real = mean over the 30 A3_real_m1 trials of mn9_hz; each null draw = its one trial's mn9_hz
definitions.pair_index: index(drive, w) = DRIVES.index(drive) x 5 + GRID_W.index(w), DRIVES = (sugar, blind); drive and cut arms are blind
definitions.missing_arm: the scorer refuses to score if a registered (non-top-up) arm is missing: it fails safe, never PASS
definitions.a4_reset: A4 runs under the v-only reset only; if B1 adopts v-and-g, the A4 readings describe the gen-5 dynamics
definitions.context: results/gen6_phaseA/preflight.json: every transform and cut on the pinned data, committed before registering

criteria.deviation: A3's bar (at least 95 of 100 draws) differs from Phase 1b's MS2 (every one of 20), and was proposed after MS2 came out at 19 of 20; MS2 is not re-scored (M4)
